docs.title: Introduction
docs.text:
The purpose of this datasheet is to document the work that has been put into the design of the main controlling subsystem. This website includes the block diagram, components, bill of materials, schematic, and power budget of this subsystem.

The main controller subsystem is essentially the "brain" of the entire system. It takes in data from the motor controller subsystem, the heat and load subsystem, and the host computer, before calculating how the arm can move in order to achieve the desired position. The calculated inputs are then sent to the motor controller subsystem.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The main subsystem includes the following attributes in its block diagram:

  • This subsystem will use 5V at 1.5A
  • This subsystem doesn't have a local sensor, however it will utilize sensor data from the Motor Encoder subsystem and the Load/Heat Subsystem
  • This subsystem doesn't have a local actuator, however it has 3 LEDs which will indicate the status of the subsystem
  • This subsystem is connected through 2 pins to the Motor Driver and Motor Encoder subsystems
  • It is also connected to the Load/Heat subsystem via 4 pins
  • This subsystem will be connected directly to a host computer for motion inputs
  • The power for the subsystem will be derived from the host computer's USB port

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
This schematic is design to function as the main processor for the robotic arm controller. The PIC18F57Q43 Curiosity Nano will be connected to a host computer via USB-c, and power will be supplied to the board via a barrel jack port on the PIC. The barrel jack's power is sent through a voltage regulator in order to be converted to 5VDC. The power produced by the voltage regulator is passed through a fuse in order to protect the board.

There are three LEDs on the board, which will be used to inform the user what the status of the board is. The three LEDs give the option of up to 8 different codes based on the pattern that the LEDs are lit. Each of the LEDs is fed power through signal ports RF1-RF3, and the signals pass through a 100 ohm resistor in order to protect the LEDs

Signals from the three other subsystems are sent to the 1x8 pin connectors in the diagram (although in the actual design we will be using 2x4 pin connectors), which are then passed directly to their respective ports as outlined in the box diagram. The ground pins for each of the 1x8 connectors are linked together, and are subsequently tied to a ground port on the Curiosity Nano.
